summary: Completed the research phase: reviewed primary method and research-process sources, inspected the fixed protocol and fixture, and passed the non-training fixture check. No models were trained.
issues: An initial evidence-hash audit used an incorrect relative root; corrected it, and the final JSON and evidence-hash validation passed.
objective: Establish the prior-work context, inspect the immutable study protocol and fixture, and record research-phase observations without training.
predictions: The registered directional hypothesis predicts a positive mean paired test-accuracy difference for weight decay 0.01 versus 0.
A paired conditional 95% bootstrap interval wholly below zero would contradict that directional hypothesis; an interval spanning zero would be inconclusive, not evidence of equivalence.
The shuffled-label control is expected to perform worse than models trained with real labels; this remains prospective.
alternatives: Weight decay has no measurable effect under this fixed setup.
An apparent effect reflects training variation or an implementation or metric error.
observations: The fixture check passed with shape [1797, 64] and split sizes of 1078 train, 359 validation, and 360 test examples.
The reviewed code uses a shared [64, 128, 10] ReLU MLP and varies the registered AdamW weight_decay setting across neural arms.
No training or evaluation results exist from this phase.
Final evidence-ledger hashes and relevant JSON files validated successfully.
learning: AdamW literature motivates testing decoupled weight decay but does not establish a positive effect for this specific MLP and digits split. The fixed example-level split, three seeds, and model-conditional bootstrap limit generalization and uncertainty claims.
rationale: This phase gathered relevant prior work, checked the supplied fixture, and documented prospective predictions and alternatives while preserving the protocol and leaving outcome evaluation to later phases.

summary: Completed the preregister phase. Recorded the fixed prospective study plan and verified the supplied protocol remained unchanged. No training was performed.
objective: Prospectively specify the fixed AdamW weight-decay comparison, alternatives, outcome analysis, falsification rule, data boundaries, and run budget.
predictions: The directional hypothesis predicts a positive mean across-seed test-accuracy difference for decay 0.01 versus decay 0.
A paired conditional 95% bootstrap interval wholly below zero contradicts the directional hypothesis; an interval crossing zero is inconclusive, not evidence of equivalence.
The shuffled-label control is expected to lose useful predictive accuracy relative to real-label training.
Recomputed metrics from saved held-out labels, predictions, and example IDs should agree with recorded accuracies.
alternatives: Weight decay has no material effect under this fixed setup.
An apparent effect reflects training variation, finite test-sample variation, or an implementation or measurement error.
observations: The required non-training fixture check passed: shape [1797, 64], with 1078 training, 359 validation, and 360 test examples.
The supplied protocol fixes the architecture, optimizer, seeds, data partition, primary metric, bootstrap procedure, controls, pilot ordering, and budget.
The preregistration cites the AdamW paper and official PyTorch, scikit-learn, and research-process sources.
No pilot, comparative training, or test outcome was produced in this phase.
The evidence ledger validates all six entries and their SHA-256 hashes.
learning: Prior work motivates testing AdamW's decoupled weight decay but does not determine its effect on this particular MLP and split. The fixed example-level split, three seeds, and model-conditional bootstrap constrain interpretation.
rationale: The preregistration makes the directional prediction and its falsification criterion explicit while preserving the supplied protocol. The analysis distinguishes inconclusive results from evidence of equivalence and limits claims to the fixed study setting. Supporting sources include [Loshchilov and Hutter](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05101), [PyTorch AdamW documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html), [scikit-learn digits documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.datasets.load_digits.html), and [Neel Nanda's research-process guide](https://www.alignmentforum.org/s/5GT3yoYM9gRmMEKqL).

summary: Completed the core phase: strengthened the non-training fixture check, documented the reproduction procedure and registered comparisons, and recorded the check command and evidence hashes. The fixed protocol is unchanged.
objective: Implement and document the fixed study's core reproduction path and meaningful pre-training checks without training or changing the registered protocol.
predictions: The registered primary hypothesis predicts a positive mean paired test-accuracy difference for weight decay 0.01 versus 0.
The preregistered conditional bootstrap interval wholly below zero would contradict that directional hypothesis; an interval spanning zero would be inconclusive.
The shuffled-label arm is expected to perform worse than real-label training, as a control diagnostic.
alternatives: Weight decay has no material effect under this fixed setup.
An apparent effect may reflect training variation, finite test-sample variation, or implementation or measurement error.
observations: The registered `study.py check` command passed: dataset shape [1797, 64], split sizes 1078/359/360, and model probe output shape [2, 10]. No training was performed.
Evidence ledger hashes validated, and the supplied protocol hash still matches its registration.
Official PyTorch and scikit-learn documentation were checked for AdamW behavior, dataset details, and stratified splitting.
learning: The supplied fixture supports a simple, auditable check before training. AdamW's decoupled decay and the reproducible split are grounded in their official documentation, but those facts do not determine whether decay improves accuracy in this specific study.
rationale: The check now validates expected split sizes and class coverage and performs a finite-output MLP forward pass without fitting. The reproduction guide documents the pilot-before-comparisons handoff, baselines, control, sensitivity arm, and limits of the registered analysis. Training remains deferred to the controller's later phases.
